newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-SAINT-ANDRE SEEKS EXPERIENCE RATHER THAN MONEY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SAINT-ANDRE SEEKS EXPERIENCE RATHER THAN MONEY.

text.p: Former France captain Philippe Saint-Andre will seek experience rather than cash when he turns out for English club Gloucestershire next season.
"I wanted to know professional rugby, the real (thing), and for me that meant England," said Saint-Andre, who turned down an offer from Paris club Stade Francais. "It's not for economic reasons.
"It was the best way to detach myself completely from my non-sporting activities and dedicate myself 100 percent to rugby."
The speedy and elusive Montferrand winger, who has captained his country in 29 of his 63 internationals, will start training with Gloucester at the end of June after house hunting in the area in May.
He missed this year's Five Nations' campaign after an operation for a groin injury.
Saint-Andre joins a number of illustrious compatriots in the English league, including World Cup team mates Philippe Sella, Thierry Lacroix and Laurent Cabannes.
Saint-Andre said he has known Gloucester coach Richard Hill, England's scrum-half in the 1991 World Cup final, since France's Five Nations' tournament match against England that year.
"During the (last) winter, while I was recovering from my operation, he sought me out. He said to me: 'I want to strengthen my team and I need a bloke like you.' That's when the discussions began."
Saint-Andre's injury has given him to time to consider his future carefully.
"By being away from the stadiums, I realised I had until I was 60 or more to work but I didn't have as much time to play rugby," said the publicity company director, who turned 30 on April 19.

"The arrival of professionalism is a chance for me to live my passion to the full by getting completely involved. For that, I have two or three years left, a period in which I only want to think about rugby with the hope of playing in the next World Cup," he said.
"I know French rugby perfectly and I don't believe there's anything it can give me that I don't already know.

"And also, in fact, I'm too comfortable at Clermont. It's time for me to try something new and break my habits. To go abroad, discover a new way of life and learn a new language is a challenge I can face thanks to rugby."
Saint-Andre is the first player signed by Hill, who is bidding to put Gloucester among the top English clubs in the next two years.
"Hill told me he wanted a three-quarter capable of passing on his experience to the whole line of attack and also give them some French spirit," Saint-Andre said.
